note: Each case carries a 'fn' selector alongside input/want. familyOf lowercases before matching (case-insensitive, unlike HistoryPricing.priceFor) and checks substrings in a fixed order fable>opus>sonnet>haiku, so an id matching two of them resolves to whichever comes first. colorForFamily/textOnFamilyFill pin the dark-ramp '3 - i' index flip (the two ramps are stored in opposite prominence order). textOnFamilyFill's 'Other' branch resolves to an actual hex (white/ink) same as any known family. colorForFamily's 'Other' branch is DIFFERENT: the web returns the literal, un-resolved CSS variable string 'var(--graydot)' — spelled here in that literal web vocabulary per this directory's README, and identical for both dark:true/false (the web function never branches on dark for this slot) — a pure Swift port has no CSS to resolve against, so its own colorForFamily instead resolves this slot outright to the graydot token's hex; readers translating this vector Swift-side must map the literal 'var(--graydot)' want to that resolved hex, not compare it as a string. sequentialColor pins that the light stops are the light ramp REVERSED while the dark stops are the dark ramp AS-IS, plus t-clamping outside [0,1] and the interpolated midpoint (t=0.5).

cases.name: familyOf: fable substring
familyOf: case-insensitive opus match
familyOf: sonnet substring
familyOf: haiku substring
familyOf: ambiguous id resolves to the earlier family in fixed order
familyOf: unknown model keeps its verbatim original-case id
colorForFamily: Fable light
colorForFamily: Fable dark uses index 3-0=3
colorForFamily: Opus light
colorForFamily: Opus dark uses index 3-1=2
colorForFamily: Sonnet light
colorForFamily: Sonnet dark uses index 3-2=1
colorForFamily: Haiku light
colorForFamily: Haiku dark uses index 3-3=0
colorForFamily: Other returns the literal graydot CSS var, unresolved, light
colorForFamily: Other returns the SAME literal graydot CSS var in dark (no dark branch for this slot)
textOnFamilyFill: Fable light is white
textOnFamilyFill: Fable dark uses index 3-0=3, ink
textOnFamilyFill: Opus light is white
textOnFamilyFill: Opus dark uses index 3-1=2, ink
textOnFamilyFill: Sonnet light is ink
textOnFamilyFill: Sonnet dark uses index 3-2=1, ink
textOnFamilyFill: Haiku light is ink
textOnFamilyFill: Haiku dark uses index 3-3=0, white
textOnFamilyFill: Other light falls through to ink
textOnFamilyFill: Other dark falls through to white
sequentialColor: light t=0 is the reversed ramp's first stop
sequentialColor: dark t=0 is the dark ramp's first stop as-is
sequentialColor: light t=1 is the reversed ramp's last stop
sequentialColor: dark t=1 is the dark ramp's last stop as-is
sequentialColor: light t=0.5 interpolates the middle segment
sequentialColor: dark t=0.5 interpolates the middle segment
sequentialColor: t below 0 clamps to the t=0 result
sequentialColor: t above 1 clamps to the t=1 result
